evidence.claim: Harrison’s earlier economy depended on water as well as rails: the lake and its two major rivers carried timber out of the forests, and millions of board feet were stored in the lake at town.
evidence.quote: Millions of board feet of timber were stored in the lake at Harrison. Lake Coeur d’Alene and the St. Joe and Coeur d’Alene rivers were the major transportation routes for timber coming out of the areas forests.

evidence.claim: Harrison’s earlier economy depended on water as well as rails
evidence.quote: A branch of the O.R. & N. Railroad from Tekoa, Washington, to Harrison was completed in 1890 and was a prime factor in the development of Harrison.

evidence.claim: The Coeur d’Alene River crossing comes before Harrison; beyond town, Idaho 97 heads southeast through the Coeur d’Alene Reservation to Idaho 3.
evidence.quote: The highway travels northwest through the reservation, passing Kootenai Junior/Senior High School, towards Harrison on the shores of Lake Coeur d'Alene. SH-97 turns northeastward within Harrison and leaves the reservation by crossing over the Coeur d'Alene River.

evidence.claim: Bald eagles feed on kokanee in Lake Coeur d’Alene, with Wolf Lodge Bay a place to watch that seasonal gathering.
evidence.quote: A popular seasonal activity is viewing the bald eagles as they feed on the kokanee in the lake, mainly from the Wolf Lodge Bay.

evidence.claim: December and January are the peak eagle-watching months along the shore between Wolf Lodge Bay and Beauty Bay.
evidence.quote: Eagle watching is great in December and January between Wolf Lodge Bay and Beauty Bay. Wildlife is expansive and diverse throughout the year, eagle watching at its peak in December and January.

evidence.claim: The fish have their own history in these waters: kokanee were stocked by the Idaho Department of Fish and Game.
evidence.quote: Kokanee, chinook, and rainbow trout were stocked by the Idaho Department of Fish and Game.

evidence.claim: Kokanee were introduced to improve fishing; native fish in the lake included bull trout, westslope cutthroat and whitefish.
evidence.quote: These fish species were not historically native to the lake, but were introduced to improve fishing.  Bull trout, westslope cutthroat, and whitefish were all native to the lake

evidence.claim: This bay also marks the highway’s northern end, where Idaho 97 meets Interstate 90.
evidence.quote: SH-97 ends at a diamond interchange with Interstate 90 at the east end of Wolf Lodge Bay.

evidence.claim: Construction began in 1963; National Recreation Trail designation followed in 1982.
evidence.quote: Construction began on the trail in 1963 and the area was designated as a National Recreation Trail in 1982.

evidence.claim: The 3.3-mile route has a self-guided interpretive tour, with learning stations explaining local plants and animal life.

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Land Management administers this backcountry hiking area near Lake Coeur d’Alene.
evidence.quote: Mineral Ridge National Recreation Trail is a backcountry hiking area near Lake Coeur d'Alene in Kootenai County, Idaho, United States.  It is administered by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM).

evidence.quote: the route travels south along the eastern shoreline of Lake Coeur d’Alene, home to bald eagles and the largest population of nesting osprey in the Western states.
